criteria.test: The thesis section states Judgment: conditionally durable for NVIDIA AI-driven revenue over the twelve months after 2026-10-05, names the horizon end 2027-10-05, and calls that judgment an inference or an estimate, not a fact.

At least one verified Data Center revenue claim for the latest eligible quarter cites a full-text primary company source with a locator, and every claim whose metric class is revenue, growth, margin, or concentration does the same.
The thesis identifies AI-driven revenue with the disclosed Data Center segment and does not describe consolidated total revenue as AI-driven revenue.
Every numeric claim records an applicable period, every comparison claim names two different periods, and no claim uses a retrieval timestamp as its applicable period.

The invalidation section states at least two conditions, and each condition names a metric, a direction, a threshold that is a sourced or code-reconciled number, and the source id that defines the metric.
The opposing-evidence section contains at least two claims tied to source ids from opposing sources, and the countercase does not assert that the two sides are equally weighted.
The alternatives section states two distinct alternatives, and each one cites a source id and uses only numbers present in claims.
Every numeric claim is unit-reconciled in code: money comparisons convert millions and billions to USD before relating them, and no numeric claim is marked unreconciled.
Every inference or estimate claim lists supporting fact ids that resolve to fact claims, and the report does not label an inference as a fact.
Every source record has an id, title, publisher, retrieval timestamp, and a publication value that is an ISO date or the token unknown. Unknown is not rewritten as a date.
The monitoring section lists at least three observables whose dates fall after 2026-10-05, each with a source id.
No used source has a known publication date after 2026-10-05 or a publication value of unknown, and at least one used source predates the cutoff and keeps its own publication date.
Every verified numeric claim has a locator, and each sourced number is present in the cited passage under unit reconciliation or reproduced by the claim formula from cited inputs.
Bad behavior: a report or countercase line contains a dollar amount or a percent and does not contain a source id that owns that amount.
Bad behavior: a numeric claim or a reported magnitude is neither present in a cited passage under unit reconciliation nor reproduced by the recorded formula from cited inputs.
Bad behavior: the working rubric ids, tests, weights, critical flags, axes, or polarities differ from the frozen mandate rubric.
Bad behavior: the report or countercase contains an order, broker instruction, account access, position size, or an invented return.
Bad behavior: a claim is marked verified when a cited source is missing or its availability is not full_text.
